newsitem.title: CHINA: China petrochemical firms see profit fall in '96.
newsitem.headline: China petrochemical firms see profit fall in '96.

text.p: The profits of three of the four major petrochemical companies in eastern China dropped sharply in 1996 due to duplication of facilities, the official Economic Daily said on Wednesday.
However, officials attributed the profit drop to reasons such as sluggish market demand and rising international prices for crude oil.

Over capacity and lack of cooperation had reduce the competitive strength of the four petrochemical firms based near Nanjing, capital of eastern Jiangsu province, and eroded profits, the Economic Daily said.

However, the newspaper did not give figures for the decline in the profits of Yizheng Chemical Fibre Co Ltd, Yangzi Petrochemical Co and Jinling Petrochemical Co. The Nanjing Chemical Industrial Corp reportedly made a profit.

Citing problems of over capacity, the newspaper said Yizheng Chemical Fibre, under the Chinese General Association of Textile Industry, planned to expand its PTA capacity to 600,000 tonnes before the year 2000 from a current 20,000 tonnes a year to meet its own demand, it said.

Yangzi Petrochemical Co, a subsidary of the China National Petrochemical Co (Sinopec), with 600,000 tonnes of existing PTA production capacity could not sell its output to Yizheng and was now devloping its refining capacity, it said.

However, the refining capacity of Yangzi had already reached 5.0 million tonnes a year while Jinling Petrochemical Co, also a Sinopec subsidiary, had refining capacity of 7.0 million tonnes, it said. Both were already unable to work at full capacity because of shortages of raw materials, it said.
However, an official of Yangzi attributed the drop in profits to sluggish market demand rather than overlapping output.
Pre-tax profits of Yangzi fell to 1.554 billion yuan this year from 4.5 billion yuan in 1995, he said.
The pre-tax profits of Jinling declined to 1.414 billion yuan this year from 1.8 billion yuan in 1995, a company official said by telephone.
He said rising international prices of crude in 1996 and heavy loan repayments had cut into profits last year.

The profits of Yizheng dropped sharply in 1996 compared with the previous year, a company official said in a telephone interview. He refused to give a reason, saying the final profit figure would be issued in April.
